userStories.title: Verify real MCP SDK protocol negotiation
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a child-process test that spawns the mcp-adapter over stdio using the real @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@^1.30.0 client and inspects the negotiated protocol version, so that the PRD's claimed '2026-07-28' wire version is proven or disproven against actual SDK behavior instead of asserted in a constant.
acceptanceCriteria: New test in packages/mcp-adapter/test-e2e/ spawns the built adapter (StdioServerTransport from cli.ts) via the SDK's Client + StdioClientTransport and captures the negotiated protocolVersion from the initialize response
Test asserts the actual negotiated value returned by the SDK, not the PROTOCOL_VERSION constant in packages/protocol/src/version.ts
Test fails loudly (not silently passes) if negotiation errors or the client falls back unexpectedly
pnpm --filter @foundry-mcp/mcp-adapter test:e2e passes
Type-check passes
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: Use packages/mcp-adapter/test-e2e/smoke.test.ts as the harness pattern. server.connect(transport) in cli.ts:26-27 is where negotiation happens server-side; use the SDK's own Client class client-side rather than hand-rolling JSON-RPC.
userStories.notes: Implemented in iteration 1. Added packages/mcp-adapter/test-e2e/protocol-negotiation.test.ts, which spawns dist/cli.js as a real child process via StdioClientTransport + Client and taps transport.onmessage to capture the raw initialize response's protocolVersion (Protocol.connect wraps, not replaces, a pre-existing onmessage handler). Evidence: installed @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.0's SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS is ['2025-11-25','2025-06-18','2025-03-26','2024-11-05','2024-10-07'] (dist/esm/types.js) -- '2026-07-28' is NOT a version this SDK can negotiate. Since the client requests LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION and the server (server/index.js _oninitialize) echoes the requested version if supported else falls back to LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION, the actual negotiated wire version in this stack is '2025-11-25'. This feeds directly into US-002.

userStories.title: Context pack export tool + foundry:// resources
userStories.description: As an AI client, I want foundry.intelligence.context plus MCP resources (foundry://connections, foundry://world/{connectionId}, foundry://document/{uuid}, foundry://session/{uuid}, foundry://intelligence/latest), so that read-only campaign context is available as resources, not just tools.
acceptanceCriteria: foundry.intelligence.context returns a bounded context pack (reuses US-015's bounding/redaction logic) suitable for direct prompt inclusion
Each listed foundry:// resource URI is registered on the McpServer and resolves to the correct read-only data via existing tool logic (no duplicated business logic between tool and resource handlers)
Resource list is enumerable via the MCP resources/list call in a child-process test
Type-check passes
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: McpServer supports registerResource alongside registerTool (see @modelcontextprotocol/sdk server/mcp.js used in server.ts) — reuse the same handler functions where possible.

userStories.title: Optional provider-based summarization with provenance
userStories.description: As a GM, I want foundry.intelligence.summarize to optionally use a configured provider or MCP sampling to summarize/classify event batches, always recording provenance (model/provider, source event IDs, timestamp, status), so that generated intelligence is auditable and provider failure never blocks ingestion.
acceptanceCriteria: Provider/sampling failure is caught and recorded as a failed provenance record; ledger ingestion (US-025/026) continues unaffected
Every summarize call, success or failure, writes a provenance record with model/provider name, source event IDs, timestamp, and status
No summarize call can mutate Foundry documents directly — it only returns/stores a suggestion
Test simulates a provider throwing and asserts ingestion pipeline is unaffected and a failed provenance record exists
Type-check passes
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: Reuses the provider interface pattern established in US-020/US-021.

userStories.title: Permission policy engine + structured permission errors
userStories.description: As a GM, I want a policy engine enforcing read-only-by-default with scoped create/update/asset/AI-network grants per connected user, so that mutating tools are refused unless explicitly authorized, with structured PERMISSION_DENIED errors.
acceptanceCriteria: A policy module evaluates {connectionId, foundryUserRole, requestedCapability} against stored grants and returns allow/deny
All mutating tools added so far (documents.create/update, assets.upload/attach, sessions.start/append) call this policy check before performing any side effect
Denied requests return a structured PERMISSION_DENIED error including the missing capability name
Permission fixtures for Player, Trusted, Assistant, and GM roles (PRD §10) each get at least one test proving correct allow/deny
Type-check passes
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: This is the PRD §3/§10 permission-fixture requirement — centralize the check so US-031's audit log has one interception point.

userStories.title: Audit log for mutations
userStories.description: As a security-conscious GM, I want every mutating operation (and every permission denial) recorded in a local audit log, so that I can review what the AI actually did or attempted.
acceptanceCriteria: New audit table (migration, following US-025's pattern) records {timestamp, connectionId, tool, outcome (success|denied|error), correlationId}
Every call through US-030's policy engine writes an audit entry regardless of outcome
Audit entries never contain secret material (API keys, pairing secrets) even if present in the request payload — redact known secret fields
Test asserts a denied call and a successful call both produce exactly one audit row each
Type-check passes
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: Single interception point from US-030 makes this additive rather than scattered across every tool handler.

userStories.title: Real Foundry companion module: document/asset operations
userStories.description: As a GM, I want the real packages/foundry-module (beyond its current handshake-only implementation) to execute document create/update, asset upload, and event-hook emission against a real Foundry v14 client using public Foundry APIs, so that the bridge is backed by an actual Foundry module rather than only the fake runtime.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/foundry-module/src/ gains document-operation handlers that call Foundry's public generic Document APIs (create/update, embedded documents) under the connected user's permissions
Asset upload handler uses Foundry's FilePicker upload API respecting the same path/MIME/size policy validated in US-019
Hook listeners (createDocument/updateDocument/deleteDocument etc.) emit the event envelope shape defined in US-026 over the module's WebSocket bridge

Companion endpoint configuration supports ws:// for local HTTP Foundry and wss:// for HTTPS/reverse-proxied or remote Docker-hosted Foundry, with an explicit Foundry Origin allowlist and no wildcard-origin fallback

The module architecture remains browser-client based and behaves identically when Foundry v14 runs in the desktop application or a user-managed Docker container; it never reads Foundry's database or container filesystem directly
Reconnect/resume logic survives Foundry container, browser client, and Windows broker restarts without duplicate requests or event loss beyond the documented reconciliation window
Module-side code contains no direct file-system or credential access beyond what Foundry's client APIs expose (PRD §3 no-exfiltration constraint)
Tests run against the module's logic with a mocked Foundry global (game/foundry namespace stubs) since no live Foundry install is available — clearly labeled as fake/mocked evidence
Type-check passes
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: packages/foundry-module/src/handshake.ts is the only real precedent so far; packages/host/src/fake-foundry/ws-server.ts shows the host-side counterpart the module must interoperate with.

userStories.title: PowerShell install/pair/uninstall scripts
userStories.description: As a Windows GM, I want PowerShell scripts under scripts/windows/ to install the module zip into a chosen Foundry User Data directory, generate/rotate the pairing secret, print MCP client config JSON, start the host, run doctor, and uninstall only files this product owns, so that setup doesn't require manual file copying.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/windows/install.ps1, pair.ps1, uninstall.ps1 created (or equivalent naming), each idempotent and using literal quoted paths (no $HOME/$home reassignment)
uninstall.ps1 only deletes files/paths it can prove it created/owns (e.g. via a manifest written at install time) — refuses to recursively delete an unrecognized directory
Scripts support Foundry User Data paths containing spaces and Unicode (tested with a fixture path)

install.ps1 and uninstall.ps1 accept an explicit Docker bind-mounted Foundry User Data path and install/remove only the owned module directory inside that mount without invoking Docker or mutating unrelated container data

pair.ps1 prints the MCP client JSON snippet after generating/rotating the pairing secret, without ever echoing the secret in a way that lands in shell history logs beyond the intended one-time display
Type-check passes (for any TS backing these scripts) and a PowerShell script analyzer (or manual review checklist) passes
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: PRD §9 lists these exact requirements; packages/cli/src/doctor.ts pattern shows how CLI commands wrap host functionality that scripts can shell out to.

userStories.title: Extend doctor CLI for full PRD §8 checklist
userStories.description: As a GM troubleshooting setup, I want `foundry-mcp doctor` to check config permissions, DB migrations, bridge/MCP ports, Foundry module installation, active connections, and provider configuration (without printing secrets), so that setup problems are diagnosable from one command.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/cli/src/doctor.ts extended with checks for: DB migration status (US-025), Foundry module installed in the configured User Data directory, active bridge connections, and provider configuration presence (never the provider secret value itself)
Each check reports pass/fail/warn with a human-readable remediation hint

Doctor validates configured ws:// or wss:// broker/module endpoints, Foundry Origin allowlisting, TLS/mixed-content compatibility, and an explicitly configured Docker bind-mounted User Data path without requiring Docker to be running
Provider configuration check confirms presence/absence only — a test asserts no secret value ever appears in doctor output
packages/cli/test/doctor.test.ts extended to cover each new check's pass and fail path
Type-check passes
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: packages/cli/src/doctor.ts and packages/cli/test/doctor.test.ts are the existing pattern to extend, not replace.

userStories.title: Foundry module zip packaging (v14 module.json)
userStories.description: As a GM, I want a build command that produces a loadable Foundry module directory and zip with a valid module.json targeting Foundry v14, so that I can install the companion module through Foundry's normal module installation flow.
acceptanceCriteria: New CLI command (e.g. `foundry-mcp build-module`) builds packages/foundry-module into a self-contained directory with a valid module.json (compatibility.minimum/verified set for v14)
Command also produces a versioned zip artifact
`npm pack --dry-run`-equivalent content check run against the module package confirms no secrets, databases, logs, or dev-only fixtures are included
Test asserts module.json parses and contains required Foundry manifest fields (id, title, version, compatibility)

The same module directory/zip is installable through Foundry's manifest flow or copied into an explicit Docker bind-mounted Data/modules directory; packaging does not assume the Windows desktop Foundry layout
Type-check passes
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: packages/foundry-module/package.json is the source package; esbuild/tsup bundling pattern should match other packages' build scripts.

userStories.title: E2E lifecycle test against fake runtime
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want one end-to-end test that pairs the fake Foundry runtime, enumerates types/documents/images, creates a root and embedded object, uploads or generates an image and attaches it, runs a full journal session, emits a world event, waits for indexing, retrieves a context pack, and verifies persisted state after a simulated restart, so that the whole PRD-required flow has one integrated proof point.
acceptanceCriteria: Single test file (e.g. packages/mcp-adapter/test-e2e/lifecycle.test.ts) walks the entire sequence described above against the fake runtime end-to-end
Test explicitly restarts the host/daemon process (or its in-process equivalent) mid-test and asserts prior state (documents, session, events, index) survived
A container-restart simulation disconnects and reconnects the module bridge, resumes from the last acknowledged event sequence, and proves no duplicate mutation/event after reconnect
Lifecycle fixtures explicitly enumerate and write multiple runtime-defined Actor and Item subtypes plus writable/read-only asset sources
Test output/comments clearly label this as fake-runtime evidence, not live-Foundry evidence, per PRD §10's honesty requirement
pnpm test:e2e passes in CI
Type-check passes
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: Builds directly on US-028 (context pack) and US-032 (module operations) plus every prior document/asset/journal/intelligence story.

userStories.title: Security test suite (traversal, replay, oversized, wrong-world, non-GM)
userStories.description: As a security reviewer, I want a dedicated adversarial test suite covering bad/expired token, origin/host failure, path traversal, oversized payload, schema abuse, wrong-world targeting, replay/idempotency, non-GM mutation, secret redaction, and external-provider-disabled defaults, so that PRD §10's security gate has explicit, repeatable evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: One test file per category (or one well-organized suite) exercises each of the ten listed attack categories against the running fake-runtime stack
Each test asserts a structured rejection (correct error code) and that no side effect occurred (e.g. no document created, no file written)
External-provider-disabled-by-default test confirms US-021's real provider is inert with no config present
Secret-redaction test confirms no pairing secret or provider API key ever appears in a log line or MCP response across the whole suite
Type-check passes
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: Draws on guards built in US-004/005/006 (ACL/HMAC), US-012 (conflict/versioning), US-019/022 (traversal/SSRF), US-021 (provider disabled), US-024 (idempotency), US-030 (permission).

userStories.title: Documentation set + validation matrix
userStories.description: As a new user or contributor, I want architecture/threat-model docs, a tool/resource/prompt reference, a Windows quick start, module install/pair guide, image-provider and privacy notes, journal/intelligence behavior docs, a developer guide, and an explicit validation matrix distinguishing fake-runtime from real-Foundry evidence, so that the project satisfies PRD §11 and §12's documentation and honesty requirements.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/architecture.md (or equivalent) includes a data-flow diagram and threat model covering DNS rebinding, CSRF/origin, named-pipe ACLs, token theft/replay, prompt injection, SSRF, traversal, decompression bombs, malicious SVG, private-content leakage, and malicious module-socket messages
docs/tools-reference.md documents every registered tool/resource/prompt with schema and example
docs/windows-quickstart.md walks clone-through-first-successful-foundry.connections.list

A Docker-hosted Foundry guide covers explicit bind-mounted User Data/module installation, Docker Desktop and remote-host layouts, ws:// versus wss:// reverse-proxy/TLS requirements, strict Origin allowlisting, broker discovery, restart/reconnect behavior, and removal without touching world data

The Docker guide provides an overlay/example that references but never bundles a user-owned licensed Foundry image, plus an opt-in real-container smoke checklist whose unrun steps are not presented as evidence

docs/validation-matrix.md explicitly lists, per capability, whether evidence is fake-runtime or real-Foundry (real-Foundry rows marked 'not available in this environment' with the manual smoke-test procedure instead, per PRD's no-fabrication rule)
All doc code samples/commands are copy-paste runnable and were actually run once during authoring
Type-check passes
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: This is the final PRD §12 Definition-of-Done story — the final report should cite exact commands/outcomes, known limitations, and what still requires a user's live Foundry/provider credentials.
